text.title: Freelancer Rate Raise Letter Template Failure Modes
text.summary: 6 antipatterns observed when announcing a retainer rate raise. Each pairs a symptom, a root cause, and a concrete fix keyed to a rule in 01-core-rules.xml.

antipattern.symptom: The letter says the new rate applies from the next invoice; the client's finance team rejects the invoice and the sponsor has to fight for a re-approval they did not ask for.
antipattern.root-cause: No grace period; the contract's notice clause for rate changes was never read.
antipattern.fix: Set the effective date at least 30 days out, at least one full billing cycle, and no shorter than the contract notice period; restate it in the closing line.

antipattern.symptom: The only justification is inflation or "market rates"; procurement caps the increase at their standard CPI adjustment or asks for three competing quotes.
antipattern.root-cause: No value delta was pulled from the engagement record; the letter was written from the freelancer's cost base.
antipattern.fix: Lead with at least one measurable value delta from `inputs_used`; demote inflation to a secondary sentence or remove it.

antipattern.symptom: The letter offers "a rate between X and Y depending on scope"; the client anchors on X and the negotiation starts below the intended rate.
antipattern.root-cause: Uncertainty about the client's reaction leaked into the number.
antipattern.fix: State one new rate with currency and unit, the current rate beside it, and the percentage change; move any scope-based tiering into the prepared concession.

antipattern.symptom: The announcement contains "if the new rate is a problem, I can offer..."; the client takes the fallback and the headline rate is never discussed.
antipattern.root-cause: Fear of churn wrote the concession into the opening move.
antipattern.fix: Strip every fallback from the letter; record one prepared concession in the artefact for the T+7 follow-up only.

antipattern.symptom: A client worth 40% of revenue is classified churn, receives the letter anyway, and leaves; there is no pipeline to replace them.
antipattern.root-cause: Classification was skipped or done after sending; revenue concentration was never computed.
antipattern.fix: Classify every client with evidence before sending; for any client above 30% of revenue classified churn, write the replacement-revenue plan first or defer the raise.

antipattern.symptom: No reply to the letter; the next invoice carries the new rate; the client disputes it and the relationship conversation happens on their terms.
antipattern.root-cause: No follow-up was scheduled and no written acknowledgement was required before applying the rate.
antipattern.fix: Schedule the T+7 follow-up with a path per response state; apply the new rate only after written acknowledgement is recorded in the artefact.
